title: Plea seeks denial of perks to judges resigning to avoid removal; SC sends notice to Centre
author: Krishnadas Rajagopal
content_html:
The Supreme Court on Thursday (September 3, 2026) sought the Union government’s response to a writ petition seeking a direction that constitutional functionaries, including judges, who resign rather than face a transparent inquiry for misconduct, should be denied retirement perks and benefits.

A three-judge Bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant issued notice to the Centre on the petition filed by Pratik Vora, who submitted that “resignations to avoid facing a transparent procedure of removal come only because the constitutional functionaries are fully aware that even after their resignations, they will be entitled to all perks and benefits which they would have got had they completed their tenure”.

The fact said the root cause of unconstitutional and unprincipled resignations by certain constitutional authorities is the complete absence of any deterrent, monetary or otherwise.

The petition gains significance in the context of the recent resignation of Allahabad High Court judge, Justice Yashwant Varma, who was facing an inquiry and removal proceedings by the Parliament after sacks of half-burnt cash were allegedly found at his official residence when he was serving as a judge in the Delhi High Court.

“If a constitutional functionary is either elected or appointed for a particular tenure, it is his constitutional obligation to complete the tenure and discharge the constitutional obligation imposed by such election or appointment,” the petition said.

While these functionaries were otherwise protected from “arbitrary removals on the whims of any individual or on petty grounds”, they had equally a liability to complete their designated tenure in office or face the “transparent procedure of removal”.

“An easy option of resigning to avoid removal is neither contemplated nor desirable. These kinds of resignation defeat the confidence which the Constitution places upon the high constitutional functionaries,” the petition said.

Resignation to avoid a transparent process of removal amounted to a betrayal of the probity in public life expected from these functionaries, the petition pointed out

“In case of Judges occupying constitutional position, the proceedings under the Judges Inquiry Act are contemplated and for other constitutional functionaries, other procedural requirements for their removal are contemplated... Those constitutional functionaries who tender their resignations, whether to avoid any proceedings of removal or proceedings for no confidence motion, should not be entitled to the perks and all other incidental facilities attached to the constitutional office from which they have resigned,” the petition said.

title: Supreme Court dismisses plea against curbs on entry of journalists and activists in U.P., Rajasthan schools
author: Krishnadas Rajagopal
content_html:
The Supreme Court on Thursday (September 3, 2026) declined to intervene in a plea challenging restrictions put in place by the Uttar Pradesh and Rajasthan governments on the entry of journalists, social media influencers and civil rights activists into government schools, along with curbs on photography, videography, interviews, audio recording and livestreaming.

A Bench headed by Justice P.S. Narasimha said the court was not inclined to entertain the writ petition filed by Priya Mishra, represented by advocates Narendra Mishra and Aakanksha Dwivedi, under Article 32 of the Constitution against separate orders passed by the Rajasthan Director of Secondary Education on August 16 and the District Basic Education Officer, Ayodhya, Uttar Pradesh, barring outsiders from entering or videographing school premises. Similar orders were issued in Azamgarh, Ballia, Basti, Balrampur, Shamli, and Agra districts of Uttar Pradesh.

The restrictions warned that any unauthorised entry, presence, or attempts to photograph or videograph inside school premises would lead to police action. The petition said the orders explicitly cautioned that such persons would face proceedings under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, and the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012.

“The petition highlights widespread public concern regarding the substandard conditions and functioning of government schools across the country. These concerns stem from reports and public allegations detailing inadequate infrastructure, dilapidated school buildings, severe shortages of teachers, lack of basic toilet and drinking-water facilities, deficiencies in mid-day meal schemes, and the absence of other essential educational infrastructure,” Mr. Mishra submitted.

He referred to the ‘School Thik Karo’ campaign by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) to audit and improve the neglected infrastructure of government schools in rural India.

In Rajasthan, CJP members were chased away by a mob at Rampura-Kanwarpura village in Jaipur when they tried to visit a dilapidated government primary school last month. On Wednesday, the authorities reportedly bulldozed the school as it was unsafe.

“The public initiative designated as the ‘School Thik Karo’ campaign was launched with the primary objective of visiting, inspecting, and documenting the physical condition and administrative deficiencies of government schools. The record reflects that requests were received from several districts across Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh, and other States seeking independent inspections of schools suffering from inadequate infrastructure and poor upkeep,” the petition said.

It argued that the restrictions on entry were a breach of freedom to disseminate information to the public about the safety and dignity of children studying in government schools.

“The infrastructure, enrolment, attendance, mid-day meal/PM POSHAN facilities and other statutory educational facilities reflected in official records allegedly do not correspond with the actual conditions prevailing at the ground level. The restrictions, while purportedly justified in the name of protecting the privacy, safety and dignity of students, have the effect of restricting transparency, public accountability, freedom of expression, legitimate journalism and public-interest scrutiny of government schools,” the petition said.

title: BJP holds two-day workshop on water resources for Ministers from 14 party-ruled States
author: The Hindu Bureau
content_html:
The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) organised a two-day workshop on water resources, which was chaired by its president, Nitin Nabin and attended by 25 Ministers from 14 States governed by the party. The workshop was held at the BJP headquarters, and it concluded on Thursday (September 3, 2026).

At a press conference, senior BJP leader Vinay Sahasrabuddhe said the BJP’s Good Governance and Policy Research department organised the event.

Increasing effectiveness

“Experts provided guidance on effective ministerial functioning, the landscape of India’s water resources, and organisation-government relations. The objective of the workshop was to enhance the Ministers’ effectiveness, help governments achieve better outcomes, and strengthen the goal of good governance,” he said.

Mr. Sahasrabuddhe has been overseeing the department for more than a decade. It has also played a role in conferences of the BJP and National Democratic Alliance Chief Ministers.

He said the Union government had earlier convened a conference of Water Resources Ministers from all the States. “After its conclusion, this meeting and workshop commenced yesterday with an address by BJP national president Nitin Nabin,” the BJP leader said, adding that a small inaugural programme was held at Mr. Nabin’s residence.

Ministers overseeing departments such as irrigation, rural drinking water and, in some cases, drinking water and sanitation, attended the workshop. Mr. Nabin interacted with the Ministers and shared his thoughts.

title: Congress’s criticism of GDP figures is a ‘dimagi Naxal’ mindset: BJP
author: The Hindu Bureau
content_html:
The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) on Thursday (September 3, 2026) accused the Congress of using faulty calculations to convert India’s 7.8% real GDP growth into an “imaginary” 2.6%, terming it a “dimagi Naxal” mindset.

The rebuttal came after Congress general secretary (communications) Jairam Ramesh asked why GDP estimates for all four years since 2022-23 had been revised substantially downwards, what components of the new methodology had driven the changes, who had been consulted in framing it, and why the deflator used for calculating real GDP appeared to understate the impact of inflation.

The questions were raised days after the government highlighted 7.8% real GDP growth in the April-June 2026 quarter.

In response, BJP chief spokesperson Anil Baluni told PTI , “Jairam Ramesh’s entire three-page statement rests on comparing two numbers that cannot be compared. Everything built upon that error collapses with it.”

He said: “If India grows slowly, it declares the government a failure. If India grows rapidly, it declares the data fraudulent. If economic indicators improve, it searches for one weak number. If the arithmetic refuses to support its politics, it simply changes the arithmetic.”

“That is the ‘dimagi Naxal’ mindset: an inability to accept Indian achievement, accompanied by a constant urge to diminish it, discredit it and damage the confidence of Indians themselves,” he said.

The latest example was the attempt to convert India’s 7.8% real GDP growth in Q1 FY2026-27 into an “imaginary” 2.6%, and then into “basically zero”, the BJP MP said.

“The trick is: take last year’s GDP from the old, discontinued 2011-12-base series. Compare it with this year’s GDP from the new 2022-23-base series. Divide one by the other. Call the resulting number India’s “real growth”. Then subtract household inflation from it,” said Mr. Baluni.

Citing data, Mr. Baluni said rebasing did not begin with Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s tenure. “This is not the first time India has revised its GDP base year. It is the ninth such revision since Independence. Between 1956 and 1999 alone, five revisions were carried out, and in total five revisions took place when Congress was in power at the Centre,” he said.

“Were those revisions intended to mask structural stagnation, low productivity, and slow expansion of the Indian economy between the 1950s and early 1990s? The truth is that base revisions are routine statistical exercises undertaken to improve accuracy and reflect structural changes in the economy,” said Mr. Baluni.

He said the Congress’s arguments about the reduction of ₹43 lakh crore in the estimated size of the economy were “statistical theatre” and “slogan”.

“...MoSPI has not concealed the reduction. It published old-series and new-series comparisons, sector-wise changes and detailed explanations for them,” he said, adding that a negative manufacturing deflator did not mean prices fell. “Manufacturing and consumption did not contract. The claim that manufacturing contracted by 5.2% and private consumption fell by 5.4% repeats the same cross-series mistake,” he added.

Mr. Baluni accused the Congress of misusing the International Monetary Fund (IMF) rating, saying the IMF’s 2025 assessment did assign India’s national accounts a C rating, but it did not declare the country’s GDP growth data fraudulent as the Congress was presenting it.

title: Gig work a full-time job for many in India, finds survey
author: The Hindu Bureau
content_html:
A nationwide survey by a non-governmental organisation, Janpahal, has found that platform work has become a long-term form of employment in the country. Nearly 57% of workers, surveyed by the organisation, said they worked more than 49 hours a week, while almost 23% worked over 70 hours. It added that more than 72.3% have remained on platforms for over one year, including 38.4% for more than two years and 18.4% for over five years.

The 84-page report, titled ‘Occupational Safety and Health of Platform-based Gig Workers in India: Report on a Nationwide Survey’, added that India’s rapidly expanding platform economy is being sustained by millions of workers who face unsafe working conditions, excessive working hours, increasing climate-related risks, inadequate social protection, and limited access to even basic workplace facilities.

The NGO said it surveyed 1,000 platform workers across 10 Indian cities to understand the working conditions of food delivery workers, ride-hailing drivers, e-commerce delivery personnel, and workers engaged in household and personal care services.

Also Read | Majority of India’s gig workers remain out of the government’s reach

It noted that workers lacked access to basic workplace facilities. “Nearly 74.6% reported having no access to rest areas. 53.8% had to purchase drinking water using their own money. 66.2% rarely or never took breaks during working hours. 43.9% relied on paid public toilets, 15% had no toilet access while working, and 11.3% depended on restaurants or customers’ homes to use washrooms,” it said. Also, 62.2% of workers experienced near-miss road accidents, 27% reported traffic accidents while working, and 38% suffered injuries caused by poor road conditions.

More than 34.1% of workers experienced harassment, abuse or violence while working, while 26.6% witnessed similar incidents involving fellow workers, demonstrating that occupational risks extend well beyond road accidents.

“64.5% reported fatigue and sleep disruption, 47.4% suffered musculoskeletal pain, 41.1% experienced stress and anxiety, 30% reported eye strain, and 26.5% suffered respiratory problems associated with prolonged outdoor work and pollution. Yet 68.4% reported receiving no health-related support from the platforms they work for,” it added.

Janpahal demanded urgent reforms to ensure safe and dignified working conditions for platform workers and recommended legal recognition of platform workers as workers with enforceable rights; implementation of occupational safety and health standards; access to toilets, drinking water, rest areas and shaded spaces; climate-responsive workplace policies; statutory mechanisms to promote workers’ voices and stronger accountability of digital labour platforms for the safety and well-being of the workers.

title: On Uttam Kumar’s birth centenary, West Bengal CM vows to keep politics out of Tollywood
author: Shrabana Chatterjee
content_html:
West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari on Thursday said the government will leave politics out of the Bengali film industry while launching the birth centenary celebrations of late actor Uttam Kumar.

“I assure you that the State government will not interfere in anything. There will be no politics. I want everything to be transparent. There is talent and I want that talent to receive proper nourishment,” Mr. Adhikari said while addressing one of the largest gatherings to celebrate the event at Tollygunge, home to the Bengali film industry.

At the event, organised next to one of the tallest statues of Uttam Kumar in the city, the CM said the Bengali film industry in its heyday was one of the best in the country. He added that renovation would be undertaken at institutions named after the actor as part of the celebrations.

Actor-turned-Trinamool Congress MP Dev (Deepak Adhikari); actors Prosenjit Chatterjee, Rituparna Sengupta, and Jeet; and director Haranath Chakraborty were among the top artistes present at the event.

During the tenure of the previous Trinamool Congress government, several artistes and the party were accused of “politicising” the Bengali film industry.

The government is holding a four-day celebration to commemorate the life and works of the actor popularly known as the ‘Mahanayak’ of Bengali cinema. Uttam Kumar was born on September 3, 1926 in north Kolkata and died aged 53 on July 24, 1980.

Kolkata was decked up on Thursday, with roads from the actor’s home to Tollygunge filled with murals, cut-outs, and cultural events to honour his contributions to the industry.

Some old single-screen cinema halls were also decked up as part of the celebrations. A stretch of the walls outside the Tollygunge metro station, also known as the Mahanayak Uttam Kumar station, was painted with graffiti highlighting the famous films and dialogues of the actor.

Mr. Adhikari also noted that Prime Minister Narendra Modi had paid tribute to the actor in a social media post. “Mahanayak Uttam Kumar... a legend whose timeless performances connect with people across generations. Tributes on his birth centenary,” Mr. Modi wrote on social media.

The Prime Minister had spoken about the late actor in his ‘Mann Ki Baat’ radio programme on August 30.

Film centre, stamp

Mr. Adhikari will lay the foundation stone for the Uttam Kumar Film Centre in New Town on Friday. India Post will also launch a special postage stamp commemorating the actor. The Uttam Kumar Film Festival will also kick-start at Nandan, with Nayak, Satyajit Ray’s celebrated 1966 movie starring Uttam Kumar.
